_comment: Issue/PR numbers that are NOT this repo's, and the repo each belongs to.
A bare `#N` means THIS repo — that is what a reader assumes and what
GitHub autolinks. Every number below was written bare while meaning
somewhere else, which was a dead link until this repo's numbering
climbed past it and turned each one into a live link to an unrelated,
plausible, wrong page. #458 is the write-up; laterite-dev#475 alone was
cited in two dozen files.
This is a FROZEN set, and its scope is exactly that: it holds the tree
against re-introducing a number already known to be foreign. It cannot
see a NEW bad reference — checking that needs the API, which is why
`check_issue_refs.py` reports how many bare refs it looked at and had no
opinion on rather than implying it judged them.
Every entry was verified by fetching it: the satellite numbers all
resolve in niko86/laterite-dev with a title matching what the citing
text says about them, and the six foreign ones likewise. Two of those
six were misattributed in #458's own table (3108/7194 are polars, not
arrow-rs) and are recorded here as what they are.
NOT here on purpose: `#1024` in web/eslint.config.js, which is not a
reference at all — it is an example inside that file's comment about
telling issue refs apart from hex colours.
AN ENTRY LEAVES THIS SET THE DAY THIS REPO'S NUMBERING REACHES IT, and
`check_issue_refs.py` is what executes that now (#498). It derives a
watermark — the highest PR number merged into the default branch, read off
the squash-merge convention that puts it at the end of every merged subject
— and releases every number at or below it. Both repos really do have an
issue at those numbers; what changes at the watermark is which one a BARE
reference means, and past it, it means ours.
So THIS LIST IS NO LONGER PRUNED BY HAND, and the ten that had been pruned
reversal: each was correctly released at the time, by an edit, and the point
of deriving the rule is that the edit was the defect. The list is now what it
says it is — every number cited here that the satellite also owns — and the
watermark decides which of them are still foreign. It was pruned three times
in one sitting before this; on the old form it would have needed an edit on
roughly every PR until the numbering passed the top of the range.
`claimed_through` below is the one thing git cannot see: a freshly-filed
ISSUE has a number no commit carries until the next PR merges past it. Set
it only when a bare reference to such an issue is actually being flagged,
and expect it to go stale harmlessly — the gate takes whichever of the two
is higher, so a forgotten override is overtaken rather than obeyed.

satellite.note: Same owner, private. Qualified rather than linked: a 404 is honest about being unreachable, where a bare number actively lies.
